المحاضرة 8 · ورقة مراجعة

الفصل 8: JavaScript 1 — أساسيات اللغة

المتغيرات والأنواع والكائنات والدوال والنطاق: الأساس لكل تفاعل في صفحات الويب.

01 نظرة عامة

ما موضوع المحاضرة؟

الفصل 8 من Connolly & Hoar: JavaScript 1: أساسيات اللغة. ما هو JavaScript ودوره (العميل، مزايا وعيوب، التاريخ، Web 2.0 وAJAX)، أين يوضع (inline وembedded وexternal وdefer وnoscript)، المتغيرات والأنواع (let وconst وvar، الأولية والمرجعية)، المخرجات، الشروط والحلقات وtry...catch، المصفوفات والكائنات (الحرفية، التفكيك، spread، JSON)، ثم الدوال (تعريف وتعبير وسهمية، افتراضي وrest، التداخل والرفع، callbacks، this والمُنشئات) والنطاق والإغلاق.

Chapter 8 of Connolly & Hoar: JavaScript 1: Language Fundamentals. What JavaScript is and its role (client side, pros and cons, history, Web 2.0 and AJAX), where it goes (inline, embedded, external, defer, noscript), variables and types (let, const, var; primitive vs reference), output, conditionals, loops and try...catch, arrays and objects (literals, destructuring, spread, JSON), then functions (declarations, expressions, arrows, default and rest parameters, nesting and hoisting, callbacks, this and constructors), scope and closures.

الفكرة الأساسية

JavaScript لغة ديناميكية الأنواع حيث الدوال كائنات: تُخزن في متغيرات، تُمرر كمعاملات (callbacks)، وتتذكر نطاقها (closures). افهم الفرق بين القيمة والمرجع، وlet/const/var، و== مقابل ===.

JavaScript is dynamically typed and functions are objects: stored in variables, passed as arguments (callbacks), and remembering their scope (closures). Understand value vs reference, let/const/var, and == vs ===.

قائمة المفاهيم الأساسية

  • دور JavaScript (3–10)
  • أماكن الكود (11–13)
  • المتغيرات والأنواع (14–22)
  • النصوص والشروط (23–27)
  • الحلقات والأخطاء (28–31)
  • المصفوفات (32–35)
  • الكائنات وJSON (36–44)
  • الدوال (45–60)
  • النطاق والإغلاق (61–65)
  • JavaScript's role (3–10)
  • Where code goes (11–13)
  • Variables and types (14–22)
  • Strings and conditionals (23–27)
  • Loops and errors (28–31)
  • Arrays (32–35)
  • Objects and JSON (36–44)
  • Functions (45–60)
  • Scope and closures (61–65)

المهارات المكتسبة

  • اختيار let أو const أو var بشكل صحيح.
  • توقع نتيجة == و=== وtruthy/falsy.
  • إنشاء مصفوفات وكائنات وتفكيكها.
  • كتابة دوال بثلاث صيغ وتمرير callbacks.
  • تحديد ما يراه كل سطر حسب النطاق.
  • شرح الإغلاق بمثال.
  • Choose let, const or var correctly.
  • Predict == vs === and truthy/falsy results.
  • Create and destructure arrays and objects.
  • Write functions three ways and pass callbacks.
  • Tell what each line can see by scope.
  • Explain a closure with an example.

لماذا يهم؟

كل تفاعل في صفحة حديثة (قوائم، نماذج، بيانات مباشرة) مكتوب بـ JavaScript، وهي أيضًا لغة الخادم (Node.js) والتطبيقات؛ هذا الفصل هو الأساس لكل ما بعده (DOM، الأحداث، React).

Every interaction on a modern page (menus, forms, live data) is JavaScript, which also runs servers (Node.js) and apps; this chapter is the base for everything after (DOM, events, React).

الشريحة 03 — What Is JavaScript and What Can It Do?

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • JavaScript: it is an object-oriented, dynamically typed scripting language
    • Variables are objects in that they have properties and methods
    • Unlike more familiar object-oriented languages Such as Java, C#, and C++, functions in JavaScript are also objects.
    • JavaScript is dynamically typed (also called weakly typed) in that variables can be easily (or implicitly) converted from one data type to another.
  • Primarily it is a client-side scripting language as well (Node.js, a popular server-side implementation of JavaScript!).

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

OO allows developers to use OO principles like: 1. Encapsulation (bundling data and methods into objects). 2. Inheritance (creating new classes that inherit properties and behaviors from existing ones) .3. Polymorphism (allowing different classes to be treated as instances of a common superclass, often through method overriding or overloading). 4. Abstraction (hiding complex implementation details behind simpler interfaces).

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. JavaScript: it is an object-oriented, dynamically typed scripting language

    لغة نصية كائنية ديناميكية الأنواع.

    An object-oriented, dynamically typed scripting language.

  2. Variables are objects in that they have properties and methods

    المتغيرات كائنات لها خصائص ودوال.

    Variables are objects with properties and methods.

  3. Unlike more familiar object-oriented languages Such as Java, C#, and C++, functions in JavaScript are also objects.

    حتى الدوال كائنات، بعكس Java وC#.

    Even functions are objects, unlike Java and C#.

  4. JavaScript is dynamically typed (also called weakly typed) in that variables can be easily (or implicitly) converted from one data type to another.

    ديناميكية (ضعيفة) الأنواع: التحويل ضمني.

    Dynamically (weakly) typed: implicit conversion.

  5. Primarily it is a client-side scripting language as well (Node.js, a popular server-side implementation of JavaScript!).

    أساسًا في العميل، وأيضًا في الخادم (Node.js).

    Mainly client-side, also server-side (Node.js).

الشرح — شرح موسّع

JavaScript ليست Java رغم الاسم. التحويل الضمني يفسر لماذا "9" == 9 صحيح (الشريحة 24).

JavaScript is not Java despite the name. Implicit conversion explains why "9" == 9 is true (slide 24).

الخلاصة

كائنية، ديناميكية، نصية.
Object-oriented, dynamic, scripting.

الشريحة 04 — Client-Side Scripting

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Client-side scripting refers to the client machine (i.e., the browser) running code locally rather than relying on the server to execute code and return the result.
  • A client machine downloads and executes JavaScript code
  • Other languages are Flash, VBScript and Java (Some are work in certain browsers, while others require plugins to function)

الشريحة 05 — Client-Side Scripting: Advantages

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Processing can be off-loaded from the server to client machines, thereby reducing the load on the server.
  • The browser can respond more rapidly to user events than a request to a remote server ever could, which improves the user experience.
  • JavaScript can interact with the downloaded HTML in a way that the server cannot, creating a user experience more like desktop software than simple HTML ever could.

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

1. tasks like validation and simple calculations like counting items in the shopping cart are performed in client side 2. Instant respons to user events (e.g., clicks, keypresses, mouse movements) without needing to send a request to a remote server and wait for a response 3. The server can only generate and send static HTML; it cannot directly interact with the page once it’s loaded in the browser. JavaScript, however, can update the page without requiring a full reload, enabling dynamic and interactive features.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Processing can be off-loaded from the server to client machines, thereby reducing the load on the server.

    تخفيف الحمل عن الخادم.

    Less load on the server.

  2. The browser can respond more rapidly to user events than a request to a remote server ever could, which improves the user experience.

    استجابة أسرع.

    Faster response.

  3. JavaScript can interact with the downloaded HTML in a way that the server cannot, creating a user experience more like desktop software than simple HTML ever could.

    تجربة تشبه برامج سطح المكتب.

    A desktop-like experience.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

3 مزايا: الحمل، السرعة، التفاعل.

3 advantages: load, speed, interactivity.

الخلاصة

3 مزايا.
3 advantages.

الشريحة 06 — Client-Side Scripting: Disadvantages

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • There is no guarantee that the client has JavaScript enabled, meaning any required functionality must be implemented redundantly on the server.
  • JavaScript-heavy web applications can be complicated to debug and maintain.
  • JavaScript is not fault tolerant. Browsers are able to handle invalid HTML or CSS. But if your page has invalid JavaScript, it will simply stop execution at the invalid line.
  • While JavaScript is universally supported in all contemporary browsers, the language (and its APIs) is continually being expanded. As such, newer features of the language may not be supported in all browsers.

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Why people disable javascript? a lot of ads written in JS, js track user behaviour and collect data Solutions: 1.1. Build the core functionality of the application using server-side rendering and HTML, ensuring it works without JavaScript. Then, enhance the experience with JavaScript for users who have it enabled.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. There is no guarantee that the client has JavaScript enabled, meaning any required functionality must be implemented redundantly on the server.

    قد يكون معطلًا؛ كرر الوظائف المهمة على الخادم.

    It may be disabled; repeat required features on the server.

  2. JavaScript-heavy web applications can be complicated to debug and maintain.

    صعب التصحيح والصيانة.

    Hard to debug and maintain.

  3. JavaScript is not fault tolerant. Browsers are able to handle invalid HTML or CSS. But if your page has invalid JavaScript, it will simply stop execution at the invalid line.

    لا يتسامح مع الأخطاء: يتوقف عند السطر الخاطئ.

    Not fault tolerant: stops at the bad line.

  4. While JavaScript is universally supported in all contemporary browsers, the language (and its APIs) is continually being expanded. As such, newer features of the language may not be supported in all browsers.

    الميزات الجديدة قد لا تُدعم في كل المتصفحات.

    New features may not be supported everywhere.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

العيب الأول هو سبب قاعدة الفصل 5: التحقق على الخادم دائمًا.

The first disadvantage is the reason for Chapter 5's rule: always validate on the server.

الخلاصة

4 عيوب.
4 disadvantages.

الشريحة 07 — JavaScript’s History

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • JavaScript was introduced by Netscape in their Navigator browser back in 1996.
  • Netscape submitted JavaScript to Ecma International in 1997, ECMAScript is simultaneously a superset and subset of the JavaScript programming language.
  • The Sixth Edition (or ES6) was the one that introduced many notable new additions to the language (such as classes, iterators, arrow functions, and promises)
  • The latest version of ECMAScript is the Eleventh Edition (generally referred to as ES11 or ES2020)

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. JavaScript was introduced by Netscape in their Navigator browser back in 1996.

    Netscape، متصفح Navigator، 1996.

    Netscape, Navigator browser, 1996.

  2. Netscape submitted JavaScript to Ecma International in 1997, ECMAScript is simultaneously a superset and subset of the JavaScript programming language.

    1997: إلى Ecma؛ ECMAScript هو المعيار.

    1997: to Ecma; ECMAScript is the standard.

  3. The Sixth Edition (or ES6) was the one that introduced many notable new additions to the language (such as classes, iterators, arrow functions, and promises)

    ES6: classes، iterators، arrow functions، promises.

    ES6: classes, iterators, arrow functions, promises.

  4. The latest version of ECMAScript is the Eleventh Edition (generally referred to as ES11 or ES2020)

    الأحدث (وقت الكتاب): ES11 / ES2020.

    Latest (at the book's time): ES11 / ES2020.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

ES6 = ES2015، وهو الأهم: منه let وconst والدوال السهمية وtemplate literals.

ES6 = ES2015, the most important one: it brought let, const, arrow functions and template literals.

الخلاصة

1996، 1997، ES6، ES2020.
1996, 1997, ES6, ES2020.

الشريحة 08 — JavaScript and Web 2.0

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Since it is launched to the middle of 90s Java script has limited uses such as graphic rollovers, pop-up alert messages, opening new browser windows, and validating user data in online forms.
  • After the middle of 2000s Asynchronous JavaScript And XML (AJAX) enabled sites that JavaScript became a much more important part of the development of the interactive web pages that asynchronously consume data from external web APIs.
    • XML almost replaced with JSON in the last decade

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Since it is launched to the middle of 90s Java script has limited uses such as graphic rollovers, pop-up alert messages, opening new browser windows, and validating user data in online forms.

    في البداية: استخدامات محدودة (تأثيرات، تنبيهات، نوافذ، تحقق).

    At first: limited uses (rollovers, alerts, windows, validation).

  2. After the middle of 2000s Asynchronous JavaScript And XML (AJAX) enabled sites that JavaScript became a much more important part of the development of the interactive web pages that asynchronously consume data from external web APIs.

    منتصف 2000s: AJAX جعل JavaScript أساسيًا لصفحات تجلب البيانات بشكل غير متزامن.

    Mid-2000s: AJAX made JavaScript central for pages fetching data asynchronously.

  3. XML almost replaced with JSON in the last decade

    JSON حل محل XML تقريبًا.

    JSON has mostly replaced XML.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

غير متزامن = الصفحة تجلب بيانات دون إعادة تحميل كاملة.

Asynchronous = the page fetches data without a full reload.

الخلاصة

AJAX ← Web 2.0.
AJAX → Web 2.0.

الشريحة 10 — JavaScript in Contemporary Software Development

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • JavaScript’s role has expanded beyond the constraints of the browser
  • It can be used as the language within server-side runtime environments such as Node.js.
  • MongoDB use JavaScript as their query language
  • Adobe Creative Suite and OpenOffice use JavaScript as their end-user scripting language
  • ….

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

Figure: JavaScript beyond the browser (transcribed)
Use
Creates sophisticated desktop-like user experiences within the browser.
Creates browser extensions.
Author non-browser applications for other platforms (using Ember/React Native/Electron, etc.).
Bundled as scripting language in other non-browser applications.
Many new programming languages can be transcompiled into JavaScript.
Create Command-Line Interface (CLI) tools.
There is a huge infrastructure of JavaScript libraries and frameworks.
Can create browser-based games and virtual reality experiences.
Server-side development environments (e.g., Node.js).
Query languages within noSQL databases.
Control language for Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices.
Available in many microcontrollers and embedded systems.

    دور JavaScript تجاوز المتصفح.

الشريحة 11 — Where Does JavaScript Go?

  • Embedded JavaScript refers to the practice of placing JavaScript code within a <script> element .
  • Placing the script in an external file with a js extention (the recommended way) via the <script> tag

الشريحة 12 — Adding JavaScript to a page

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

[Title only; the content is the figure.]

<html lang="en">
<head>
   <title>JavaScript placement possibilities</title>
   <script>                                              <- Embedded JavaScript
      /* A JavaScript Comment */
      alert("This will appear before any content");
   </script>
   <script src="greeting.js"></script>                  <- External JavaScript
</head>
<body>
<h1>Page Title</h1>
<a href="JavaScript:OpenWindow();">for more info</a>    <- Inline JavaScript
<input type="button" onClick="alert('Are you sure?');" />
<script>                                                 <- Embedded JavaScript
   alert("Hello World");
</script>
<h2>Other Content</h2>
...
<script defer src="helpers.js"></script>                <- External JavaScript
</body>
</html>

/* defer: This optional flag tells browser to defer parsing this JavaScript until the rest of
   page is loaded. This can improve the speed at which the page elements first appear in the browser. */

helpers.js
function calculateTotal (price, quantity) {
   let subtotal = price * quantity;
   return subtotal;
}
function calculateTax(total) {
   return total * 0.10;
}
/* Notice that an external JavaScript file contains no markup. */

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

High-traffic sites will embed styles and JavaScript within the HTML to speed up performance by reducing the need for extra HTTP requests. In these cases performance improves because the size of the embedded styles and JavaScript are quite modest For maintainability reasons, <script> elements are usually placed within the <head> element (and for performance reasons, after any CSS <link> elements). For performance reasons, some scripts are placed at the end of the document, just before the </body> closing tag (examples for this will be shown in the next chapter).

defer: downloads the file but runs it after the whole page is parsed, so the page appears faster. And an external file contains no HTML tags.

الشريحة 14 — Variables and Data Types

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Variables in JavaScript are dynamically typed, meaning that you do not have to declare the type of a variable before you use it.
  • To declare a variable in JavaScript, use either the var, const, or let keywords (see Table 8.1) or even without any one
  • Assignment can happen at declaration time by appending the value to the declaration, or at runtime with a simple right-to-left assignment

                  // Each line of JavaScript should be terminated with a semicolon.

foo= 4 ;          // foo is assigned the value of 4, Notice that whitespace is unimportant,
foo  =
   "hello"   ;    // foo is assigned the string value of "hello".
                  // Notice that a line of JavaScript can span multiple lines.

الشريحة 18 — Data Types

  • JavaScript has two basic data types:

الشريحة 19 — Primitive Types

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Boolean True or false value.
  • Number Represents some type of number. Its internal format is a double precision 64-bit floating point value.
  • String Represents a sequence of characters delimited by either the single or double quote characters.
  • Null Has only one value: null.
  • Undefined Has only one value: undefined. This value is assigned to variables that are not initialized. Notice that undefined is different from null.
  • Symbol New to ES2015, Symbol can be used when it is important that variables are not equal, even though their value and type are the same.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Boolean True or false value.

    Boolean: صح/خطأ.

    Boolean: true/false.

  2. Number Represents some type of number. Its internal format is a double precision 64-bit floating point value.

    Number: عدد عشري 64 بت.

    Number: 64-bit float.

  3. String Represents a sequence of characters delimited by either the single or double quote characters.

    String: نص بين ' أو ".

    Undefined: لمتغير بلا قيمة؛ يختلف عن null.

الشريحة 20 — Primitive vs Reference Types

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Primitive variables contain the value of the primitive directly within memory.
  • In contrast, object variables contain a reference or pointer to the block of memory associated with the content of the object.

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

let abc = 27;
let def = "hello";        // variables with primitive types
let foo = [45, 35, 25];   // variable with reference type (i.e., array object)
let xyz = def;
let bar = foo;            // these new variables differ in important ways (see below)
bar[0] = 200;             // changes value of the first element of array

Memory representation:
abc [27]  def ["hello"]  xyz ["hello"]   Each primitive variable contains the value directly within the memory for that variable.
foo [*]--+--> [45][35][25]   memory for foo object instance
bar [*]--+    This element will get changed to the value of 200. Thus, both foo[0] and bar[0] will have the same value (200).
Each reference variable contains a reference to the memory that contains the contents of that object.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Primitive variables contain the value of the primitive directly within memory.

    الأولي يحمل القيمة نفسها.

    A primitive holds the value itself.

  2. In contrast, object variables contain a reference or pointer to the block of memory associated with the content of the object.

    الكائن يحمل مرجعًا (مؤشرًا) للذاكرة.

    An object variable holds a reference (pointer).

الشرح — شرح موسّع

لذلك: xyz = def ينسخ «hello»، أما bar = foo فينسخ المرجع فقط؛ تغيير bar[0] يغير foo[0] أيضًا (200).

So: xyz = def copies “hello”, but bar = foo copies only the reference; changing bar[0] changes foo[0] too (200).

الخلاصة

نسخ القيمة / نسخ المرجع.
Copy value / copy reference.

الشريحة 21 — Let vs const

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

[Title only; the content is the figure.]

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

// All of these let examples work with no errors.
let abc = 27;              abc = 35;
let message = "hello";     message = "bye";
let msg = "hello";         msg = "hello";
let foo = [45, 35, 25];    foo[0] = 123;   foo[0] = "this is ok";
let person = {name: "Randy"};   person.name = "Ricardo";
person = {};

// Some of these const examples work won't work, but some will work.
const abc = 27;            abc = 35;              // Will generate runtime exception, since you cannot reassign a value defined with const.
const message = "hello";   message = "bye";       // Will generate runtime exception.
const msg = "hello";       msg = "hello";         // Will generate runtime exception.
const foo = [45, 35, 25];  foo[0] = 123;  foo[0] = "this is also ok";   // You are allowed to change elements of an array, even if defined with a const keyword.
const person = {name: "Randy"};   person.name = "Ricardo";   // Allowed to change properties of an object.
person = {};                                       // Will generate runtime exception.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. (figure) let examples that all work, and const examples where reassignment throws but changing array elements or object properties is allowed

    let: كل شيء مسموح. const: لا إعادة إسناد، لكن تعديل العناصر والخصائص مسموح.

    let: all allowed. const: no reassignment, but changing elements and properties is allowed.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

const يثبت الربط (المرجع) لا المحتوى. لذلك foo[0] = 123 يعمل، لكن person = {} يفشل.

const fixes the binding (reference), not the content. So foo[0] = 123 works, but person = {} fails.

الخلاصة

const = لا إعادة إسناد.
const = no reassignment.

TABLE 8.4 Comparator Operations (transcribed)
OperatorDescriptionMatches (assume x=9)
==Equals(x == 9) is true
(x == "9") is true

equivalent to*/

الشريحة 26 — The conditional (ternary) operator

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Another way to make use of conditionals is the conditional/ ternary operator (?:).

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

/* conditional (ternary) assignment */
foo = (y==4) ? "y is 4" : "y is not 4";
//    Condition  Value if true  Value if false
/* equivalent to */
if (y==4) { foo = "y is 4"; }
else { foo = "y is not 4"; }

let tip = isLargeGroup ? 0.25 : 0.15;
/* equivalent to */
let tip;
if (isLargeGroup) { tip = 0.25; }
else { tip = 0.15; }

let price = isChild ? 5 : isSenior ? 7 : 9;
/* equivalent to */
let price;
if (isChild) price = 5;
else if (isSenior) price = 7;
else price = 9;

الشريحة 28 — While and do . . . while Loops

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • While and do…while loops execute nested statements repeatedly as long as the while expression evaluates to true.
  • As you can see from this example, while loops normally initialize a loop control variable before the loop, use it in the condition, and modify it within the loop.
let count = 0;
while (count < 10) {
// do something
// ...
count++;
}
count = 0;
do {
// do something
// ...
count++;
} while (count < 10);

الشريحة 30 — Infinite Loop Note

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Infinite loops can happen if you are not careful, and since the scripts are executing on the client computer, it can appear to them that the browser is “locked” while endlessly caught in a loop, processing.

الشريحة 31 — Try…catch

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • DIVE DEEPER
  • When the browser’s JavaScript engine encounters a runtime error, it will throw an exception. These exceptions interrupt the regular, sequential execution of the program and can stop the JavaScript engine altogether. However, you can optionally catch these errors (and thus prevent the disruption) using the try . . . catch block as shown below.
  • try...catch can also be used to your own error messages.
try {
   nonexistantfunction("hello");
}
catch(err) {
   alert ("An exception was caught:" + err);
}

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

However, you can optionally catch these errors (and thus prevent the disruption) using the try . . . catch block as shown below.

    الخطأ وقت التشغيل يرمي استثناء يوقف البرنامج؛ try...catch يلتقطه.

  2. try...catch can also be used to your own error messages.

  • The second approach is to use the Array() constructor:
  • const name = new Array(value1, value2, ... );

الشريحة 36 — Objects

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • We have already encountered a few of the built-in objects in JavaScript, namely, arrays along with the Math, Date, and document objects.
  • Now, we will learn how to create our own objects and examine some of the unique features of objects within JavaScript.
  • In JavaScript, objects are a collection of properties (named values).
  • Unlike languages such as C++ or Java, objects in JavaScript are not created from classes. JavaScript is a prototype based language, in that new objects are created from already existing prototype objects, an idea that we will examine in Chapter 10.

الشريحة 40 — Object Destructuring

}

الشريحة 41 — Spread

  • It should be noted that this is a shallow copy, in that primitive values are copied,but for object references, only the references are copied.

الشريحة 47 — Function expressions

  • The object nature of functions can be further seen in the next example, which creates a function using a function expression.
  • When we invoked the function via the object variable name it is conventional to leave out the function name for so called anonymous functions
// defines a function using a function expression
const sub = function subtotal(price,quantity) {
return price * quantity;
};
// invokes the function
let result = sub(10,2);
// defines a function using an anonymous function expression

return price * quantity;
};
// invokes the function
let result = calculateSubtotal(10,2);

الشريحة 48 — Arrow Syntax

  • The arrow function version would look like the following:
    • const taxRate = () => 0.05;
  • As you can see, this is a pretty concise (but perhaps confusing) way of writing code.

Figure: Arrow syntax overview (transcribed)
Traditional syntaxArrow syntaxNotes
function () { statements }() => { statements }Multi-line function, no parameters: {}, () required

الشريحة 50 — Changes to “this” in Arrow Functions

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Arrow functions do not have their own this value (see Figure 8.22). Instead, the value of this within an arrow function is that of the enclosing lexical context (i.e., its enclosing parental scope at design time).
  • While this can occasionally be a limitation, it does allow the use of the this keyword in a way more familiar to object-oriented programming techniques in languages such as Java and C#.
  • When we finally get to React development in Chapter 11, the use of arrow functions within ES6 classes will indeed make our code look a lot more like class code in a language like Java.

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  2. While this can occasionally be a limitation, it does allow the use of the this keyword in a way more familiar to object-oriented programming techniques in languages such as Java and C#.

    Feels like Java and C#.

  3. When we finally get to React development in Chapter 11, the use of arrow functions within ES6 classes will indeed make our code look a lot more like class code in a language like Java.

    Useful in React (Chapter 11).

الشريحة 53 — Nested Functions

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • To avoid adding another identifier to the global scope, nest calculateTax inside calculateTotal .
function calculateTotal(price,quantity) {
let subtotal = price * quantity;
return subtotal + calculateTax(subtotal);
// this function is nested
function calculateTax(subtotal) {
let taxRate = 0.05;
return subtotal * taxRate;
}
}
function calculateTotal(price,quantity) {
let subtotal = price * quantity;
let taxRate = 0.05;
let tax = subtotal * taxRate;
return subtotal + tax;
}
function calculateTotal(price,quantity) {
let subtotal = price * quantity;
return subtotal + calculateTax(subtotal);
}
function calculateTax(subtotal) {
let taxRate = 0.05;
return subtotal * taxRate;
}

الشريحة 54 — Hoisting in JavaScript

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Function declarations are hoisted to the beginning of their current level
  • Also, variables defined with var are hoisted meanwhile assignments are NOT.

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

function calculateTotal(price,quantity) {
   let subtotal = price * quantity;
   return subtotal + calculateTax(subtotal);   // "Is it acceptable to use calculateTax before it is defined?"

   function calculateTax(subtotal) {           // Function declaration is hoisted to the beginning of its scope.
      let taxRate = 0.05;
      let tax = subtotal * taxRate;
      return tax;
   }
}
// This works as expected.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Function declarations are hoisted to the beginning of their current level

  2. Also, variables defined with var are hoisted meanwhile assignments are NOT.

    var variables are hoisted, but assignments aren't.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

لذلك استدعاء calculateTax قبل تعريفه يعمل. أما var x = 5 فقبل سطره x = undefined. (let وconst لا يمكن استخدامها قبل سطرها: خطأ.)

That's why calling calculateTax before its definition works. With var x = 5, before that line x is undefined. (let and const can't be used before their line: error.)

الرفع: الدوال وvar.

الشريحة 55 — Callback Functions

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Since JavaScript functions are full-fledged objects, you can pass a function as an argument to another function.
  • Callback function is simply a function that is passed to another function.

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

const calculateTotal = function (price, quantity, tax) {
   let subtotal = price * quantity;
   return subtotal + tax(subtotal);     // 2 The local parameter variable tax is a reference to the calcTax() function
};
const calcTax = function (subtotal) {
   let taxRate = 0.05;
   let tax = subtotal * taxRate;
   return tax;
};
let temp = calculateTotal(50,2,calcTax);   // 1 Passing the calcTax() function object as a parameter
// We can say that calcTax variable here is a callback function.

    this يعتمد على السياق.

    this depends on context.

  3. Luckily right now, we don’t have to do anything so complex to understand the this in the example

    هنا بسيط: this = الكائن الذي يحتوي الدالة.

    Here it's simple: this = the object holding the function.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

ملاحظة: الشكل يستخدم this.type لكن product ليس فيه type (في القائمة 8.13 اسمه brand)، فالنتيجة ستكون "undefined $500".

Note: the figure uses this.type but product has no type (Listing 8.13 calls it brand), so the result would be "undefined $500".

الخلاصة

this = الكائن المالك.
this = the owning object.

الشريحة 59 — Object Creation (iii) Using Function constructors

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • The main problem with the object literal approach lies in situations in which we want numerous instances with the same properties and methods
  • The key difference between using a function constructor and calling a regular function resides in the use of the new keyword before the function name.
// function constructor
function Customer(name,address,city) {
this.name = name;
this.address = address;
this.city = city;
this.output = function () {
return this.name + " " + this.address + " " + this.city;
};
}
// create instances of object using function constructor
const cust1 = new Customer("Sue", "123 Somewhere", "Calgary");
alert(cust1.output());
const cust2 = new Customer("Fred", "32 Nowhere St", "Seattle");
alert(cust2.output());
LISTING 8.14 Defining and using a function constructor

  1. The main problem with the object literal approach lies in situations in which we want numerous instances with the same properties and methods

    مشكلة الصيغة الحرفية: إنشاء نسخ كثيرة متشابهة.

    The literal's problem: many similar instances.

  2. The key difference between using a function constructor and calling a regular function resides in the use of the new keyword before the function name.

    الفرق: الكلمة new.

    The difference: the new keyword.

  3. LISTING 8.14 Defining and using a function constructor

    القائمة 8.14.

    Listing 8.14.

الاسم بحرف كبير (Customer) عُرف للمُنشئات.

A capitalised name (Customer) is the convention for constructors.

new Customer(…).
new Customer(…).

الشريحة 60 — What happens with a constructor call of a function

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

[Title only; the content is the figure.]

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

let cust = new Customer("Sue", "123 Somewhere", "Calgary");
// 1 A brand new empty object is created and given the name cust.
// 2 Then the function is called
function Customer(name,address,city) {   // Note: it is a coding convention to capitalize the first letter of a constructor function
   this.name = name;          // 3 The new empty object is set as the context for this. Thus, the new empty object gains these property values.
   this.address = address;
   this.city = city;
}
// 4 Since there is no return, the function will end with the (no longer empty) new object being assigned to the cust variable.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. (diagram) Four steps of new Customer(...): an empty object is created, the function is called, this is set to the new object, and the filled object is assigned to cust

    4 خطوات لـ new: كائن فارغ، استدعاء، this = الكائن، إسناده.

    4 steps of new: empty object, call, this = the object, assignment.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

بدون new: this لن يكون كائنًا جديدًا والدالة تُرجع undefined.

Without new: this won't be a new object and the function returns undefined.

الخلاصة

الشريحة 61 — Scope in JavaScript

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Scope generally refers to the context in which code is being executed.
  • JavaScript has four scopes:
  • function scope (also called local scope),
  • block scope,
  • module scope (in Chapter 10)
  • global scope.

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

Labels: “Each function is like a box with a one-way window.” “Within any function, it can see out at the content of all its outer boxes.” “But an outer function can't look into an inner function.” “And functions can't see into other functions at the same level.” “All functions can see anything within global scope.” “Scope ends at global; functions can't see outside of the global box.”

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Scope generally refers to the context in which code is being executed.

    النطاق: سياق تنفيذ الكود.

    Scope: the context code runs in.

  2. JavaScript has four scopes: function scope (also called local scope), block scope, module scope (in Chapter 10) global scope.

    أربعة: دالة (محلي)، كتلة، وحدة، عام.

    Four: function (local), block, module, global.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الشكل: كل دالة صندوق بنافذة باتجاه واحد: ترى للخارج، لا للداخل، ولا الصناديق المجاورة.

The figure: each function is a box with a one-way window: it sees out, not in, and not into sibling boxes.

الخلاصة

4 نطاقات.
4 scopes.

الشريحة 62 — Block scope

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Block-level scope means variables defined within a block of code (i.e. contained within “{}” like inside loops or conditional statements) using the let or const keywords are only available within the block in which they are defined.
  • But if declared with var within a block, then it will be available outside the block.

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

// 4 Block Scope
for (let i=0; i<10;i++) {
   const tmp = "yes";
   console.log(tmp);    // outputs: yes
}
console.log(i);         // error: i is not defined
console.log(tmp);       // error: tmp is not defined
// A variable declared within a {} block using let or const will have block scope and only be available within the block it is defined.

// 3 Global Scope
for (var i=0; i<10;i++) {
   var tmp = "yes";
   console.log(tmp);    // outputs: yes
}
console.log(i);         // outputs: 10
console.log(tmp);       // outputs: yes
// A variable will be in global scope if declared outside of a function and uses the var keyword.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Block-level scope means variables defined within a block of code (i.e. contained within “{}” like inside loops or conditional statements) using the let or const keywords are only available within the block in which they are defined.

    let وconst داخل {} متاحة داخل الكتلة فقط.

    let and const inside {} live only in that block.

  2. But if declared with var within a block, then it will be available outside the block.

    var يتسرب خارج الكتلة.

    var leaks out of the block.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

بعد حلقة for (var i…) تكون i = 10 خارجها؛ مع let خطأ «i is not defined».

After for (var i…), i = 10 outside; with let it's an error “i is not defined”.

الخلاصة

let/const = كتلة؛ var = لا.
let/const = block; var = no.

الشريحة 63 — Global Scope (i)

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • A variable will be in global scope if declared outside of a function and outside of a block, regardless of the keyword used
  • If an identifier has global scope, it is available everywhere.
  • Namespace conflict
  • If the JavaScript compiler encounters another identifier with the same name at the same scope, you do not get an error. Instead, the new identifier replaces the old one!

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

// 1 Global Scope
var abc = 'fred';
function something() {
   console.log(abc);    // outputs: fred
   abc = 'sue';
}
something();
console.log(abc);       // outputs: sue

// 2 Global Scope
let abc = 'fred';
function something() {
   console.log(abc);
   abc = 'sue';
}
something();
console.log(abc);

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. A variable will be in global scope if declared outside of a function and outside of a block, regardless of the keyword used

    عام: خارج أي دالة وكتلة، بأي كلمة.

    Global: outside any function and block, any keyword.

  2. If an identifier has global scope, it is available everywhere.

    متاح في كل مكان.

    Available everywhere.

  3. Namespace conflict: If the JavaScript compiler encounters another identifier with the same name at the same scope, you do not get an error. Instead, the new identifier replaces the old one!

    تعارض الأسماء: الاسم الجديد يحل محل القديم بلا خطأ.

    Namespace conflict: the new name silently replaces the old.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

في المثالين: abc يطبع fred داخل الدالة، ثم sue بعد استدعائها. (ملاحظة: إعادة تعريف let بنفس الاسم في نفس النطاق تعطي خطأ؛ الاستبدال الصامت يحدث مع var والدوال.)

In both examples: abc prints fred inside the function, then sue after the call. (Note: redeclaring a let with the same name in the same scope is an error; silent replacement happens with var and functions.)

الخلاصة

قلل المتغيرات العامة.
Minimise globals.

الشريحة 64 — Function/ Local Scope

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • dentifiers defined within a function have local scope, meaning that they are only visible within that function, or other functions nested within it.
  • Functions nested within other functions have access to the variables of the containing or outer function(s)

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

// Anything declared inside this block is global and accessible everywhere in this block
let c = 0;              // 1 global variable c is defined
outer();                // 2 global function outer() is called
function outer() {      // Anything declared inside this block is accessible everywhere within this block
   function inner() {   // Anything declared inside this block is accessible only in this block
      console.log(a);   // 5 local (outer) variable a is accessed - allowed, outputs 5
      let b = 23;       // 6 local (inner) variable b is defined
      c = 37;           // 7 global variable c is changed - allowed
   }
   let a = 5;           // 3 local (outer) variable a is defined
   inner();             // 4 local function inner() is called
   console.log(c);      // 8 global variable c is accessed - allowed, outputs 37
   console.log(b);      // 9 undefined variable b is accessed - not allowed: generates error or outputs undefined
}
📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Output:

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. dentifiers defined within a function have local scope, meaning that they are only visible within that function, or other functions nested within it.

    المعرفات داخل الدالة محلية.

    Identifiers inside a function are local.

  2. Functions nested within other functions have access to the variables of the containing or outer function(s)

    الدالة الداخلية ترى متغيرات الخارجية.

    Inner functions see the outer function's variables.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الترتيب في الشكل مرقم 1–9: inner ترى a (5) وتغير c العام (37)، لكن outer لا ترى b. (dentifiers ينقصها I.)

The figure's order is numbered 1–9: inner sees a (5) and changes the global c (37), but outer can't see b. (“dentifiers” is missing an I.)

الخلاصة

الداخل يرى الخارج.
Inner sees outer.

الشريحة 65 — Closures in JavaScript

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Scope in JavaScript is sometimes referred to as lexical scope
  • The ending bracket of a function is said to close the scope of that function. But closure refers to more than just this idea.
  • A closure is actually an object consisting of the scope environment in which the function is created; that is, a closure is a function that has an implicitly permanent link between itself and its scope chain.

Footer: Pearson — Copyright © 2021, 2018, 2015 Pearson Education, Inc. All Rights Reserved

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

let g2 = "variable with global scope";
function parent2() {
   let foo2 = "within parent2";
   function child2() {
      let bar2 = "within child2";
      return foo2 + " " + bar2;
   }
   return child2;     // Notice that we are not invoking the inner function now.
                      // Instead, we are returning the inner function (and not its return value as in previous example).
}
let temp = parent2();
alert("temp = " + temp);       // The temp variable is now going to contain inner child2() function.
                               // Alert: temp = function child2() { let bar3 = "within child2"; return foo2 + " " + bar2; }
alert("temp() = " + temp());   // The temp function still has access to the foo2 variable within the parent2 function even
                               // though the temp function is now outside its declared lexical scope (i.e., the parent2 function).
                               // Alert: temp() = within parent2 within child2
console.dir(temp);             // It has this same access since the closure keeps a record of the lexical (design-time) scope environment.
                               // DevTools: temp f child2() > [[Scopes]]: Scopes[3] > 0: Closure (parent2) foo2: "within parent2"
                               //           > 1: Script g2: "variable with global scope" > 2: Global

Side notes on the slide: “After parent2 executes, we might expect that any local variables defined within the function to be gone (i.e., garbage collected). Yet in this example, this is not what happens. The local variable foo2 sticks around even after parent2 is finished executing. Why? This happens because the parent2 function has a closure. A closure is like a special object that contains a function's design-time scope environment. A closure thus lets a function continue to access its design-time lexical scope even if it is executed outside its original parent.”

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Scope in JavaScript is sometimes referred to as lexical scope

    النطاق معجمي (lexical).

    Scope is lexical.

  2. The ending bracket of a function is said to close the scope of that function. But closure refers to more than just this idea.

    قوس الإغلاق يغلق النطاق، والإغلاق أكثر من ذلك.

    The closing brace closes the scope; closure is more.

  3. A closure is actually an object consisting of the scope environment in which the function is created; that is, a closure is a function that has an implicitly permanent link between itself and its scope chain.

    الإغلاق: دالة تحتفظ برابط دائم مع نطاقها وقت الإنشاء.

    A closure: a function keeping a permanent link to its creation scope.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

المثال: parent2 تنتهي لكن temp (أي child2) ما زالت ترى foo2، فتعطي «within parent2 within child2». (التنبيه الأول في الشكل يعرض bar3 بدل bar2.)

The example: parent2 finishes but temp (child2) still sees foo2, giving “within parent2 within child2”. (The first alert in the figure shows bar3 instead of bar2.)

الخلاصة

الدالة تتذكر مكان ولادتها.
A function remembers where it was born.

05 ثلاثة مستويات

  • HTML الهيكل، CSS الطلاء، JavaScript الكهرباء التي تشغل الأشياء.
  • المتغير صندوق باسم؛ const صندوق مقفل الغطاء لكن يمكن تغيير ما بداخله إن كان كائنًا.
  • المصفوفة رف مرقم من 0؛ الكائن خزانة أدراج بأسماء.
  • الدالة وصفة؛ callback وصفة تعطيها لطباخ آخر.
  • الإغلاق: حقيبة ظهر تحملها الدالة فيها متغيرات المكان الذي وُلدت فيه.
  • HTML is the frame, CSS the paint, JavaScript the electricity that makes things work.
  • A variable is a named box; const is a box with a locked lid, but if it holds an object you can still change what's inside.
  • An array is a shelf numbered from 0; an object is a chest of named drawers.
  • A function is a recipe; a callback is a recipe you hand to another cook.
  • A closure: a backpack the function carries with the variables of the place it was born.
  • الأنواع: 6 أولية (تُنسخ بالقيمة) وكائنات (تُنسخ بالمرجع)؛ const يثبت الربط لا المحتوى؛ var نطاق دالة ويُرفع، let/const نطاق كتلة.
  • المقارنة: == مع تحويل ضمني، === صارم؛ falsy: false، null، undefined، 0، NaN، "".
  • التحكم: if/else، switch (break)، ?:، while، do...while، for، for...of، try...catch.
  • البيانات: [ ] و{ }، النقطة والأقواس، التفكيك، spread (نسخ سطحي)، JSON.parse/stringify.
  • الدوال: declaration (تُرفع)، expression، arrow (this معجمي، return ضمني)، default، rest، nested، callbacks، constructors مع new، النطاقات الأربعة، والإغلاق.
  • Types: 6 primitives (copied by value) and objects (copied by reference); const fixes the binding not the content; var is function-scoped and hoisted, let/const are block-scoped.
  • Comparison: == with implicit conversion, === strict; falsy: false, null, undefined, 0, NaN, "".
  • Control: if/else, switch (break), ?:, while, do...while, for, for...of, try...catch.
  • Data: [ ] and { }, dot and bracket access, destructuring, spread (shallow copy), JSON.parse/stringify.
  • Functions: declarations (hoisted), expressions, arrows (lexical this, implicit return), default, rest, nested, callbacks, constructors with new, the four scopes, and closures.
  • const افتراضيًا، let للتغيير، تجنب var.
  • === دائمًا.
  • falsy: false null undefined 0 NaN "".
  • `${x}`.
  • for (let x of arr).
  • let [a,b] = arr؛ let {a,b} = obj.
  • ...spread = نسخ سطحي.
  • JSON: "key"؛ JSON.parse.
  • () => value.
  • (a=1)، (...args).
  • الدوال وvar تُرفع.
  • callback = دالة كمعامل.
  • new + this.
  • closure = دالة + نطاقها.
  • const by default, let to change, avoid var.
  • Always ===.
  • falsy: false null undefined 0 NaN "".
  • `${x}`.
  • for (let x of arr).
  • let [a,b] = arr; let {a,b} = obj.
  • ...spread = shallow copy.
  • JSON: "key"; JSON.parse.
  • () => value.
  • (a=1), (...args).
  • Functions and var are hoisted.
  • callback = function as argument.
  • new + this.
  • closure = function + its scope.

    07 نصائح احترافية

    كيف تفهم بدل أن تحفظ

    • افتح وحدة التحكم (F12 ← Console) وجرب كل سطر من الشرائح مباشرة.
    • قبل تشغيل أي مثال، اكتب توقعك ثم قارن.
    • لكل متغير اسأل: قيمة أم مرجع؟ ولكل سطر: أي نطاق يراه؟
    • اقرأ الدالة السهمية بصوت: «تأخذ a وتُرجع …».
    • Open the console (F12 → Console) and try each line from the slides directly.
    • Before running an example, write your prediction, then compare.
    • For each variable ask: value or reference? For each line: which scope can it see?
    • Read an arrow function aloud: “takes a and returns …”.

    تمارين عملية مقترحة

    1. أعد مثال الشريحة 20 وغيّر bar[0] وراقب foo.
    2. جرب جدول let/const في الشريحة 21 سطرًا سطرًا.
    3. اكتب subtotal بالصيغ الثلاث (declaration، expression، arrow).
    4. اكتب calculateTotal مع callback (55–56).
    5. أعد مثال الإغلاق (65) وافحصه بـ console.dir.
    1. Rebuild slide 20's example, change bar[0] and watch foo.
    2. Try the let/const table on slide 21 line by line.
    3. Write subtotal three ways (declaration, expression, arrow).
    4. Write calculateTotal with a callback (55–56).
    5. Rebuild the closure example (65) and inspect it with console.dir.

    أخطاء شائعة

    • استخدام == بدل ===.
    • الظن أن const يمنع تغيير محتوى المصفوفة.
    • نسيان break في switch.
    • الظن أن "0" أو [] falsy.
    • نسيان أن الفهرس يبدأ من 0.
    • استخدام دالة سهمية كـ method تحتاج this.
    • نسيان new مع المُنشئ.
    • استخدام var داخل حلقة وتوقع نطاق كتلة.
    • Using == instead of ===.
    • Thinking const stops changing an array's contents.
    • Forgetting break in switch.
    • Thinking "0" or [] is falsy.
    • Forgetting indexes start at 0.
    • Using an arrow function as a method that needs this.
    • Forgetting new with a constructor.
    • Using var in a loop and expecting block scope.
